set.body:
Ranked the strongest competitive differentiator available by the field-positioning reviewer, who raised it from a gap-fill to their #2 after measuring the incumbent. I never filed it.

TODAY: R/views.R:104-108 refuses. rdm() and rsa() accept a geometry plan or a complete effect form, and nothing else - so a crossnobis plan cannot be turned into an RDM through the ordinary verb. The crossnobis path and the RDM path are separate despite producing the same shape of object.

WHY IT IS THE STRONGEST MOVE AVAILABLE, measured rather than asserted:
  rsatoolbox      one call, calc_rdm(method='crossnobis')
  rMVPA           reachable ONLY as contrast_rsa_model(estimation_method='crossnobis'),
                  requires an msreve_design rather than an rsa_design, cannot be produced by
                  plain rsa_model() at all, and appears in ZERO of 29 vignettes
  effectagram     crossnobis() is already a top-level exported function with a worked example
                  and a four-line path from raw timeseries - already ahead of rMVPA - but the
                  RDM verb does not accept it

So the package is one branch away from matching rsatoolbox one-call ergonomics on the exact quantity an rsatoolbox user arrives looking for, while already beating the R incumbent on surfacing. That is a head-to-head win rather than a gap being closed, and it is available cheaply.

There is a performance dimension the reviewer measured as well: 28 plan executions taking 16.9 s today, against 0.41 s for the same 28 pairs on the identity-metric path that already exists. Whether that gap is inherent to the learned metric or is overhead worth investigating is a separate question, but it should be understood before this becomes the advertised path.

SAFETY: same rule as bd on the relation-accepting verbs. Route through the plan and the existing query-first branch, never materialize, return the existing view class.
set.title: Make the crossnobis RDM one call: rdm() and rsa() should accept a crossnobis plan
